entries.description: Get visits-over-time overview (totals + daily series) for a tracked site owned by the calling wallet.

usage.callShape: GET https://stableanalytics.dev/api/site/overview?site_id={site_id}&period={24h|7d|30d}&limit={1-500} with Sign-In-With-X header (signed by the wallet that owns the site). No per-call payment.
usage.outputShape: site_id, period, totals.visits, totals.unique_ips_estimate, series[].date, series[].visits
quirks: SIWX identity-only — NO per-call payment (accepts[] in the 402 challenge is empty); the calling wallet must OWN the site (the wallet that paid to create it via POST /api/site/create).
Unknown/unowned site_id returns HTTP 404 {success:false,error:'Site not found'} — NOT an auth failure.
period enum is exactly 24h|7d|30d (default 7d); limit 1-500 (default 100).

Test wallet owns no site (GET /api/sites => {sites:[]}); 200 body verified via OpenAPI schema, auth+call-shape verified live (404 path).

entries.name: Tech Stack Detector
entries.description: Fetch a URL and detect its full technology stack (CMS, framework, CDN, server, WAF, analytics) from HTTP response headers, HTML meta tags, cookies, and script patterns — plus a security-header score and letter grade. Wappalyzer/BuiltWith alternative, no browser required. Available via three gateways with different input conventions.

url.description: URL to fingerprint (e.g. https://example.com); bare domains are accepted and get https:// prepended. Aliases also accepted: target, domain, host, site (query param or JSON body).
Public http(s) URL to fingerprint, e.g. https://example.com — passed as the ?url= query parameter.

platform.description: e.g. wordpress, shopify, squarespace, wix, webflow, nextjs, custom-php, static-or-custom-html

category.description: cms, ecommerce, site-builder, framework, static-generator, static, custom

generator.description: raw meta generator tag when present

usage.callShape: DEFAULT (netintel): GET https://netintel-production-440c.up.railway.app/tech-fingerprint/analyze?url=https://example.com  (query param `url` = FULL URL incl. scheme; no body; x402 ~$0.002 on Base). ALT (x402-deployer): POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/tech-stack-detect with JSON body {"url":"https://example.com"} (~$0.01). ALT (hugen): GET https://domain.hugen.tokyo/domain/tech?domain=example.com (query param `domain` = BARE hostname, NO scheme; ~$0.01).
usage.outputShape: netintel returns: url, status_code, response_time_ms, detections[].{name,category,confidence}, summary.{server,cdn,cms,waf,javascript_frameworks[],analytics[]}, security_headers_present[], security_headers_missing[], score (number), grade (letter A-F), findings[].{rule,deduction,detail}
quirks: Multi-gateway: each gateway uses a DIFFERENT input field/shape — netintel=GET query `url` (full URL w/ scheme), x402-deployer=POST JSON body `url`, hugen=GET query `domain` (BARE hostname, no scheme/path). Do not cross the field names or you get a 400.
Default netintel is cheapest ($0.002 vs $0.01) AND richest: only it returns the security-header score/grade/findings; the others return detection lists only.
netintel normalizes the URL (input https://example.com → output url https://example.com/).
Synchronous single-call (no async/poll). Pure read of public site headers — safe to auto-verify.

entries.name: NetIntel Cloud Fingerprint
entries.description: Fingerprints a domain's cloud infrastructure by probing DNS records, HTTP headers, and PTR lookups to detect the CDN, WAF, hosting provider, DNS provider, and email provider with per-signal confidence scores, plus an infrastructure security score (0-100) and letter grade (A-F).

domain.description: Domain to fingerprint, e.g. cloudflare.com (bare hostname, no scheme/path). Required query parameter.

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/cloud-fingerprint/analyze?domain=<domain> (single required query param `domain`, a bare hostname like cloudflare.com; no request body). x402 paid, no API key.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous top-level JSON: .domain (echoed), .resolved_ips[] (A-record IPs), .cname_chain[], .hosting{provider,confidence,signals[]}, .cdn{provider,confidence,signals[]}, .waf[]{provider,confidence,signals[]}, .dns_provider{provider,confidence,signals[]}, .email_provider{provider,confidence,signals[]}, .http_fingerprint{https_enforced,server_header,server_version_exposed,x_powered_by,notable_headers[]}, .tls{issuer,wildcard,san_count}, .score (0-100), .grade (A-F letter), .findings[] (security findings). Result is at the top level (NOT nested under body.data).
quirks: Input is a query-string param (?domain=), not a JSON body — it is a GET. Pass a bare hostname including TLD, e.g. cloudflare.com (no scheme, no path).

Confidence is per-detection ('high' | 'medium' | ... ) with human-readable .signals[] explaining the evidence (e.g. 'cf-ray header present', 'NS ns3.cloudflare.com contains cloudflare.com'); a provider can be null with empty signals when nothing was detected (e.g. email_provider was null for cloudflare.com).
The .tls sub-object came back all-null in this probe (issuer/wildcard/san_count) even though the schema advertises them — treat TLS fields as best-effort/optional.
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.01.
Distinct from NetIntel Tech Stack Detector (/tech-fingerprint/analyze): this detects cloud/CDN/WAF/DNS/email INFRASTRUCTURE + a security grade, not the web app framework/library stack.
qa-pay reported confirmed:false / txHash:null but status 200 with the full payload — Base settlement is async; the call succeeded and is billed only on success.
usage.guide: Call GET https://netintel.dev/cloud-fingerprint/analyze with a single required query param `domain` set to a bare hostname including TLD (e.g. ?domain=cloudflare.com — no scheme, no path). It is an x402 pay-per-call endpoint at $0.01 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC) — no API key, no signup; the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON at the top level. Read .hosting / .cdn / .waf[] / .dns_provider / .email_provider — each carries {provider, confidence, signals[]} where signals[] explains the evidence; a null provider means undetected. .http_fingerprint reports .https_enforced, .server_header, .server_version_exposed, .x_powered_by and .notable_headers[]; .tls carries issuer/wildcard/san_count (best-effort, may be null). .resolved_ips[] and .cname_chain[] give the DNS resolution path. For a quick verdict read .score (0-100) and .grade (A-F). Use it to identify a domain's cloud/CDN/WAF/DNS/email infrastructure and assess its infra security posture in one call — attack-surface mapping, vendor/tech due diligence, or supply-chain recon.

entries.name: Webbersites OpenGraph Checker
entries.description: Social-share / OpenGraph audit for any page: fetches the URL and reports its OpenGraph and Twitter Card meta tags (og:title, og:image, og:description, og:url, og:type, twitter:card), the page title/description/canonical/robots, an image check, and a list of problems, warnings, and an overall verdict for how the link will render when shared.

url.description: Public URL of the page to audit (required query parameter, including scheme)
The normalized URL that was audited (echoed back, may add a trailing slash)

og.description: OpenGraph tags found (og:title, og:image, og:description, og:url, og:type, ...); empty object when none present

twitter.description: Twitter Card tags found (twitter:card, ...); empty object when none present

robots.description: The robots meta directive (null when absent)

image_check.description: Result of validating the og:image (dimensions/reachability); null when no og:image is present

problems.description: Blocking issues that break the social preview (e.g. og:title/og:image missing)

verdict.description: Overall assessment, e.g. 'broken' when problems exist

ts.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the audit was performed

usage.callShape: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/og/check?url=<url> — single required query parameter `url` (public URL of the page to audit, including scheme). No request body. x402-paid $0.001 USDC on Base (eip155:8453). Synchronous JSON response.
usage.outputShape: Top-level JSON object: .url (normalized), .meta {og{}, twitter{}, title, description, canonical, robots}, .image_check (object or null when no og:image), .problems[] (blocking issues as strings), .warnings[] (recommendations as strings), .verdict (e.g. 'broken'), .ts (ISO 8601 timestamp).
quirks: Input is a query-string parameter (?url=), not a JSON body — it is a GET request; URL-encode the url value.
The url parameter is required; omitting it returns HTTP 400.
image_check is null when the page has no og:image; it is populated (object) only when an og:image is present.
meta.og and meta.twitter are empty objects {} when the page has no OpenGraph/Twitter Card tags.
Results are URL-normalized (input https://example.org -> output url https://example.org/); HTTP vs HTTPS is treated as a different page.
The endpoint is non-mutating (read-only audit); safe for repeated calls on the same URL.
usage.guide: Audit how a page will render when shared on social platforms. Call GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/og/check?url=https://example.org with the public URL to check (no request body, x402-paid $0.001 USDC on Base). Response is synchronous JSON reporting the page's OpenGraph and Twitter Card meta tags, title/description/canonical/robots, an og:image check, plus problems[] (blocking), warnings[] (recommendations) and an overall verdict. Use for SEO/social-preview audits, link-unfurl debugging, or agent content QA.

entries.name: Webbersites Alt-Text Audit
entries.description: Audits any public web page for image alt-text issues — missing alt attributes, filename-as-alt, generic/over-long alt, unlabeled svg[role=img], image-map areas and image inputs without alternatives — for SEO and accessibility.

accepts.description: Alt-text audit for any page: finds images with missing alt attributes, flags filename-as-alt and generic alt text, over-long alt, unlabeled svg[role=img], image-map areas and image inputs without alternatives. Counts decorative alt="" separately. For SEO and accessibility agents.

url.description: Public URL of the page to audit

issues.description: Per-image issue list, each {tag, src, issue}

usage.callShape: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/seo/alt-check?url=<page URL> (x402 payment, 0.001 USDC on Base eip155:8453)
usage.outputShape: body.{url, images_total, with_good_alt, missing_alt, empty_alt_decorative, low_quality_alt, svg_img_unlabeled}, body.issues[] (each {tag, src, issue}), body.note, body.ts
quirks: GET request: pass the page under audit in the ?url= query string (URL-encoded), NOT a JSON body. The url must be a public page.
The unpaid 402 returns a free preview with only totals (images_total, missing_alt) plus the note 'Pay and retry for the per-image issue list'; the paid 200 adds the full breakdown and body.issues[].
alt="" on purely decorative images is valid and counted separately under empty_alt_decorative, not flagged as an issue.
Provider offers a half-price rate ($0.0005) if you send an X-Wallet header (or ?wallet=) for a wallet that spent >$0.001 in the last 24h; the base price is $0.001.
Verified against https://example.com, which has no images, so all counts returned 0 and issues[] was empty — shape confirmed but a real page is needed to see issues populated.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/seo/alt-check with the page to audit URL-encoded into the ?url= query parameter (e.g. ?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com). It is pure x402: the first request returns a 402 with payment requirements (0.001 USDC on Base, EIP-3009), so pay and retry with the X-PAYMENT header (@x402/fetch automates this). On success you get a synchronous 200 JSON: read the summary counts from body.images_total / with_good_alt / missing_alt / empty_alt_decorative / low_quality_alt / svg_img_unlabeled and the per-image problems from body.issues[] (each {tag, src, issue}). No API key, no accounts.
